meta.encoding: hex unless the field name says otherwise; *Base64/*B64 are standard base64 with padding

edits.name: legacy-base-add-tag
edits.pins: §6.12.2: an unclocked base clocks no unit and its clock is the floor; the added tag takes the new clock

edits.name: remove-tag-leaves-tombstone
edits.pins: §6.12.2: a removed tag keeps a clocked unit, the tombstone

edits.name: recase-is-a-write
edits.pins: §6.12.2: a new spelling of the same tag key is a write to that unit

edits.name: trusted-base-carries-its-floor
edits.pins: §6.12.2: an edit from a base applied whole keeps the base floor (#5572)

edits.name: no-base
edits.pins: §6.12.2: with no synced base an edit carries no unit clocks and is read whole at its clock (VERIFY-5529)

edits.name: edit-keeps-unit-floors-it-did-not-clock
edits.pins: §6.12.2: an edit keeps the base fieldFloors of every unit it did not change

edits.name: edit-drops-the-unit-floor-it-clocks
edits.pins: §6.12.2: a unit the edit clocks carries its write clock, not its unit floor

wholesales.name: untrusted-remote-is-its-floor
wholesales.pins: §6.12.1: an older build’s record clocks no unit, and its clock is the floor that carries its removals (#5572)

wholesales.name: stale-stamp-is-dropped
wholesales.pins: §6.12.1: unit clocks an older build kept past their stamp are not writes

wholesales.name: trusted-remote-keeps-its-own
wholesales.pins: §6.12.1: a trusted remote is kept as it arrived

wholesales.name: trusted-remote-keeps-its-field-floors
wholesales.pins: §6.12.1: a trusted remote with fieldFloors is kept as it arrived

wholesales.name: older-build-echo-of-field-floors-is-whole
wholesales.pins: §6.12.1: an older build kept fieldFloors verbatim but ticked clock, so the record is untrusted and its clock is the floor

merges.name: field-floors-concurrent-floors
merges.pins: §6.12.3: neither concurrent floor claims d, so the remote removal stands under its own unit floor, and k re-queues

merges.name: new-peer-reads-field-floors
merges.pins: §6.12.1: a trusted remote reads its fieldFloors entry for a floored unit, fieldClocksFloor for the rest

merges.name: floored-record-pulls-new-edit
merges.pins: §6.12.3: a merge of a floored record and a newer edit drops no unit floor the edit did not clock

merges.name: older-build-echo-of-field-floors-is-whole
merges.pins: §6.12.1: an older build that kept fieldFloors and ticked clock is read whole at its clock, today’s rule

merges.name: older-build-dropped-field-floors-is-whole
merges.pins: §6.12.1: an older build that dropped fieldFloors and ticked clock is read whole at its clock, today’s rule

merges.name: pre-field-floors-peer-record
merges.pins: §6.12.1: a trusted record from a build before fieldFloors reads fieldClocksFloor for every unclocked unit

merges.name: issue-5508-a-pulls-cli
merges.pins: #5508: an added tag and a concurrently set property both survive

merges.name: issue-5508-b-pulls-a-merged
merges.pins: #5508: a second concurrent add merges into the set

merges.name: issue-5508-ios-pulls-b-merged
merges.pins: #5508: the iOS removal of lm-jtag wins over the untouched unit; all four edits survive

merges.name: removal-beats-stale-readd
merges.pins: §6.12.3: a peer still holding the tag at an older unit clock does not resurrect it

merges.name: concurrent-add-and-remove-tie-remote-wins
merges.pins: §6.3 rule 5 per unit: equal totals, remote wins

merges.name: offline-tie-greater-value-wins
merges.pins: §6.12.3: a unit tie on ticks goes to the greater canonical value, so both sides agree; §6.3 rule 5’s _offline test does not apply per unit

merges.name: case-variant-keeps-local-spelling
merges.pins: §1.9.1 step 6: one unit per tag key, the spelling already here is kept

merges.name: old-build-remote-is-whole-record
merges.pins: §6.12.1: an older build ticked clock past fieldClocksAt; every unit in the union is read at its clock, so t-a, absent from it, is removed: today’s rule

merges.name: legacy-remote-without-field-clocks
merges.pins: §6.12.1: a payload with no fieldClocks names its units at its clock

merges.name: old-build-removes-tag-and-property
merges.pins: §6.12.1: an older build removed a tag and a property; a body-only local edit does not resurrect them

merges.name: legacy-remote-removes-tag-and-property
merges.pins: §6.12.1: a payload with no fieldClocks that lacks a unit removes it at its clock

merges.name: no-base-1-saves-old-build-removes
merges.pins: §6.12.1: an untrusted local side proves no unit clock; 1 body-only save(s) do not outrank an older build’s concurrent removal

merges.name: no-base-2-saves-old-build-removes
merges.pins: §6.12.1: an untrusted local side proves no unit clock; 2 body-only save(s) do not outrank an older build’s concurrent removal

merges.name: no-base-3-saves-old-build-removes
merges.pins: §6.12.1: an untrusted local side proves no unit clock; 3 body-only save(s) do not outrank an older build’s concurrent removal

merges.name: issue-5572-relay
merges.pins: #5572: the relay’s floor removes the tag the older build removed; q, a write concurrent with that record, survives

merges.name: issue-5572-relay-pulls-stale-copy
merges.pins: §6.12.3: the same pair the other way round: the local floor removes the stale copy and re-queues

merges.name: older-builds-applied-whole-then-concurrent-removal
merges.pins: §6.12.1: a record applied whole clocks no unit, so its body-only ticks do not outrank a concurrent older build’s removal

merges.name: untrusted-base-edit-then-concurrent-removal
merges.pins: §6.12.2: an edit from an untrusted base clocks only what it changed, so the base’s ticks do not outrank a concurrent removal

merges.name: local-dominates-every-unit-requeues
merges.pins: §6.5.2 P3: a local unit ahead of the remote re-queues

merges.name: null-property-is-a-value
merges.pins: §13.4 inside properties: null is a value, absence is a removal
